chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (mercy of God be upon him) said: My paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim related to me, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, on the authority of Amr ibn Shimr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, was there when there was nothing but Him. He was Light as there was no darkness in Him. He was the Truth as there was no falsehood in Him. He was Omniscient as there was no ignorance in Him. He was the EverLiving as there was no death in Him. And that is how He is today, and that is how He will remain forever.
ai.seo_question: What are the eternal attributes of Allah according to Imam al-Baqir (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) articulates the doctrine of divine simplicity, affirming that Allah’s essential attributes—Light, Truth, Knowledge, and Life—are identical with His essence and free from temporal change or opposites. It underscores the permanence of these attributes, reinforcing the Shia theological stance against anthropomorphism and emphasizing God's absolute transcendence and self-sufficiency.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 5. Muhammad ibn `Ali Majilwayh (RA) said: My paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim related to me, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al Barqi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, on the authority of `Amr ibn Shimr, on the authority of Jabir that Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) said:

Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, was there when there was nothing but Him. He was Light as there was no darkness in Him. He was the Truth as there was no falsehood in Him. He was Omniscient as there was no ignorance in Him. He was the EverLiving as there was no death in Him. And that is how He is today, and that is how He will remain forever.
